prompt: Manage an Outlook mailbox by fetching recent inbox messages, classifying and moving messages or whole threads into routing folders, marking VIP emails high importance, creating staged reply drafts, and producing a structured list of items needing replies.

results.use_case: Manage an Outlook mailbox by fetching recent inbox messages, classifying and moving messages or whole threads into routing folders, marking VIP emails high importance, creating staged reply drafts, and producing a structured list of items needing replies.
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Ensure correct mailbox scope, then enumerate folders using OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS (read response.data.value; follow response.data['@odata.nextLink'] if present).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Resolve and persist source/destination folder IDs using OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS; if nested, traverse using OUTLOOK_LIST_CHILD_MAIL_FOLDERS (use IDs, not display names).

[Required] [Step]: Retrieve triage candidates using OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS per folder with minimal select/filter; handle empty response.data.value and follow response.data['@odata.nextLink'] to collect message IDs + lightweight metadata.

[Optional (if OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS output is truncated/offloaded)] [Prerequisite]: Use COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH to extract/dedupe message IDs across paginated payloads and keep a checkpoint of processed IDs.

[Required (for write operations only)] [Prerequisite]: Present a small preview (counts + a few examples) and get explicit confirmation of the exact message ID set, destinations, and any field updates to apply.

[Required] [Step]: Move selected messages using OUTLOOK_BATCH_MOVE_MESSAGES (max 20 message_ids/call), run batches sequentially, record per-item outcomes, and retry stragglers with OUTLOOK_MOVE_MESSAGE.

[Required] [Next Step]: Apply read/unread and other triage fields (for example categories/flags) using OUTLOOK_BATCH_UPDATE_MESSAGES (apply to the final IDs you will continue referencing, typically moved IDs).

[Optional (if drafting replies is needed)] [Next Step]: Create draft replies for selected messages using OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT_REPLY (store returned draft IDs; avoid fetching full bodies unless required).

[Required] [Fallback]: If OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS fails/returns insufficient results or filters are unsupported, use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES for discovery (if supported) then re-run OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS in the resolved folder to fetch current IDs before moving/updating.
known_pitfalls: [OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS] Folder arrays are under response.data.value; cross-mailbox scope issues can surface as 404 ErrorInvalidUser or 403 ErrorAccessDenied.
[OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS] Invalid fields in select can trigger "Invalid field(s) in select parameter"; keep select minimal.
[OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES] Can fail with 400 indicating search is unsupported for some account types.
[OUTLOOK_BATCH_MOVE_MESSAGES] Hard cap of 20 message_ids per call; with response_detail='minimal' moved_message_id may be null even when success=true.
[OUTLOOK_BATCH_UPDATE_MESSAGES] Requires an 'updates' object; with response_detail='minimal' successful updates may return 204 without echoing updated fields.

OUTLOOK_QUERY_EMAILS.description: Query Outlook emails within a SINGLE folder using OData filters. Build precise server-side filters for dates, read status, importance, subjects, attachments, and conversations. Best for structured queries on message metadata within a specific folder. Returns up to 100 messages per request with pagination support. • Searches SINGLE folder only (inbox, sentitems, etc.) - NOT across all folders • For cross-folder/mailbox-wide search: Use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES • Server-side filters: dates, importance, isRead, hasAttachments, subjects, conversationId • Pagination: use the returned next_page_token (pass it back as page_token) until it is absent • Limitations: Recipient/body filtering requires OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES

top.description: Maximum number of messages to return per request (1-1000). Default is 100. IMPORTANT: For large mailboxes, paginate using `next_page_token`. Pagination example: 1) Call with top=100, 2) Read `next_page_token` from the response, 3) If present, call again passing it back as `page_token`, 4) Repeat until `next_page_token` is absent.

skip.description: Number of messages to skip for pagination. NOTE: For large result sets, prefer the returned `next_page_token` (pass it back as `page_token`) over manual skip.

examples: isRead eq false and receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z
importance eq 'high' and hasAttachments eq true
isDraft eq false and isRead eq false and importance eq 'high'
(isRead eq false or importance eq 'high') and receivedDateTime ge 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z
(isRead eq false or importance eq 'high') and hasAttachments eq true
from/emailAddress/address eq 'boss@company.com' and isRead eq false
categories/any(a:a eq 'Priority') and isRead eq false
filter.description:
OData $filter query string to filter email messages. Syntax: 'field operator value' combined with 'and', 'or', 'not'.

        **Operators:** eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge, startswith(), contains(), any()

        **String Functions:**
        - subject: contains(), startswith()
        - from/sender: startswith() and eq only. contains() is NOT supported on sender/from fields
        - endswith() is NOT reliably supported by Microsoft Graph API for message filtering

        **Filterable Fields:**
        - `isRead` - Boolean: true/false
        - `importance` - String: 'low', 'normal', 'high'
        - `subject` - String (exact match or startswith)
        - `hasAttachments` - Boolean: true/false
        - `receivedDateTime`, `sentDateTime` - DateTime (ISO 8601: 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z, NOT enclosed in quotes)
        - `conversationId` - String (exact match)
        - `categories` - Array (use any() operator: `categories/any(a:a eq 'CategoryName')`)
        - `isDraft`, `flag/flagStatus` - Boolean/String flags
        - `from/emailAddress/address`, `sender/emailAddress/address` - Sender email (ONLY 'address' is filterable, NOT 'name')

        **NOT filterable:** toRecipients, ccRecipients, bccRecipients, body/content, id — use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES for these.

        **Categories Filtering:**
        - Single: `categories/any(a:a eq 'CategoryName')`
        - Multiple (OR): Use SEPARATE any() calls: `categories/any(a:a eq 'Cat1') or categories/any(b:b eq 'Cat2')`
        - For category names containing single quotes, escape them by doubling: `categories/any(a:a eq 'Owner''s Category')`

        **Date Filtering:**
        - ISO 8601 format: 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z (no quotes around datetime values)
        - Operators: ge, gt, le, lt

folder.description: SINGLE mail folder to search within (cannot search across all folders). Well-known names (case-insensitive): 'inbox', 'sentitems', 'drafts', 'deleteditems', 'outbox', 'junkemail', 'archive', 'clutter', 'recoverableitemsdeletions'. For custom folders (e.g., 'Billing', 'Projects'), you MUST provide the folder ID (a long base64-like string like 'AAMkAGU0NTRiNDA4...'). Use OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS to get folder IDs for custom folders. Do NOT pass folder URLs or display names. IMPORTANT: To search across ALL folders, use OUTLOOK_SEARCH_MESSAGES instead (searches entire mailbox without folder restriction). NOTE: This parameter also accepts 'folder_id' as an alias for backwards compatibility.

select.description: List of message properties to include in the response (accepts comma-separated string or list). Field names are automatically normalized to correct camelCase (e.g., 'bodypreview' -> 'bodyPreview', 'hasattachments' -> 'hasAttachments'). Valid fields: id, subject, from, sender, toRecipients, ccRecipients, bccRecipients, replyTo, receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, createdDateTime, lastModifiedDateTime, hasAttachments, importance, isRead, isDraft, body, bodyPreview, uniqueBody, categories, conversationId, conversationIndex, parentFolderId, changeKey, internetMessageId, internetMessageHeaders, webLink, flag, attachments, inferenceClassification, isReadReceiptRequested, isDeliveryReceiptRequested. NOTE: 'inReplyTo' is NOT a valid property for email messages in Microsoft Graph v1.0. When not specified, returns metadata without body. Include 'body' for full content. Pass [] for all fields.

orderby.description: Sort order as comma-separated string or list (accepts 'field asc/desc' format or JSON-serialized arrays). Input is automatically normalized to correct format. Common fields: receivedDateTime, sentDateTime, subject, importance, from. NOTE: Ordering may be automatically disabled by Microsoft Graph API when using certain filters (e.g., subject exact match, conversationId) to avoid 'InefficientFilter' errors. In those cases, results will be unsorted.

user_id.description: Target user's email or 'me' for authenticated user. IMPORTANT: 'me' uses the currently connected account. For shared or delegated mailbox access, ensure the connected user has mailbox access and the app has Mail.Read.Shared. 403 errors indicate insufficient delegated/application permissions.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend any required identifier fields from the first call (the token supersedes their values). Optional filter, sort and timezone params need not be repeated; the token carries them.

OUTLOOK_BATCH_MOVE_MESSAGES.description: Batch-move up to 20 Outlook messages to a destination folder in a single Microsoft Graph $batch call. Use when moving multiple messages to avoid per-message move API calls.

user_id.description: The UPN (User Principal Name) of the user whose messages to move, or 'me' for the currently authenticated user.

message_ids.description: Array of message IDs to move. Maximum 20 items per batch (Microsoft Graph API limit). Each ID must be complete and untruncated.

destination_id.description: The destination folder ID, or a well-known folder name (e.g., 'inbox', 'deleteditems', 'drafts', 'sentitems'). If using a folder ID, it must be complete and untruncated.

response_detail.description: Controls how much each move sub-request returns from Microsoft Graph. 'minimal' (default) sets `Prefer: return=minimal` on each sub-request, so Graph returns 204 No Content per move — the response stays small even for the maximum 20 HTML messages. In this mode `moved_message_id` in each result is null even on success. 'full' omits the Prefer header so Graph returns the full moved-message body per sub-request and `moved_message_id` is populated. Use 'full' if you need to chain follow-up calls on the new message ID; otherwise stick with 'minimal' to avoid multi-MB batch responses.

OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDERS.description: Tool to list a user's top-level mail folders. Use when you need folders like Inbox, Drafts, Sent Items; set include_hidden_folders=True to include hidden folders.

top.description: Maximum number of items to return per page.

skip.description: Number of items to skip before returning results.

count.description: Include total count of matching items in the response.

filter.description: OData filter expression to filter mail folders. String values must be enclosed in single quotes (e.g., displayName eq 'Inbox'). WARNING: Microsoft Graph API does not officially document which mailFolder properties support filtering. Known unsupported properties: parentFolderId (causes ErrorInvalidProperty error). To filter by parent folder, use the child folders endpoint instead: GET /me/mailFolders/{parentFolderId}/childFolders. Properties like isHidden may work but are not guaranteed.

select.description: Comma-separated list of mailFolder properties to include in the response. Valid properties: id, displayName, parentFolderId, childFolderCount, unreadItemCount, totalItemCount, isHidden. Note: 'user_id' is NOT a valid mailFolder property and will be automatically removed if included.

orderby.description: Property to sort by, optionally followed by 'asc' or 'desc'.

user_id.description: User's id, userPrincipalName, or 'me' for the signed-in user.

page_token.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page. Omit for the first page; then pass back the `next_page_token` from the previous response, unmodified, until it is absent. Do not construct or edit it. When set, it drives pagination; resend any required identifier fields from the first call (the token supersedes their values). Optional filter, sort and timezone params need not be repeated; the token carries them.
